text:
Assistant B is better. It is concise and has a proper subject line, a clear structure, and a friendly tone. It gives three compelling reasons and acknowledges the friend's discomfort, with an offer of support, though it addresses objections only lightly.

Assistant A is long and rambling and contains irrelevant content. It includes a misinterpreted quote, claiming that knowing more makes you less likely to succeed, and it drifts into an essay on living in the present. It has no subject line and ends oddly after the sign-off. It violates the "concise" instruction and its logic is poor, though it does offer preparation help.

[[B]]
